learning: If oval progress recovers toward 0.6 or more with line losses near 1, the 16 mm footprint was blurring the centre signal, and the 40 mm span result from iteration 0 becomes a fair comparison. If progress stays near 0.4, the footprint is not the cause and the span or lead is. Compare max_error against the 0.0615 to 0.065 m plateau.
notes: Changes only the sensor footprint, 16 mm to 12 mm, from iteration 2. Gains and span are unchanged so the footprint effect can be read directly against iteration 2 (oval 0.405, s-bend 0.423).
rationale: Iteration 2 (60 mm span, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.05, kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45) recovered most of the progress lost in iteration 1. Oval progress rose from 0.273 to 0.405 and s-bend from 0.109 to 0.423, and line losses stayed at 1.0 to 1.2. Iteration 1 changed span, footprint and lead together, so the 16 mm footprint is still an unisolated suspect. Iteration 0 (12 mm footprint, 40 mm span, y = 0.05) reached 0.664 on the oval, so the footprint and span effects are not yet separated. The Builder's proposal for this iteration changes only the footprint, from 16 mm to 12 mm, and keeps the 60 mm span and y = 0.05 lead. I therefore keep the controller exactly as in iteration 2 (base 1.5, kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45, weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, last_direction). Changing gains now would confound the footprint test. Five sensors at 15 mm pitch with 12 mm footprints leave a 3 mm gap between neighbours, but the 25 mm tape is always covered by at least one footprint across the array, so I expect no dead zone that the controller cannot handle. The measurement request adds noise_robustness and completion_time so the next race can be compared with iteration 2 on the same metrics.
